catalog_quote: The Italic accent is hypothesized as fixed and not phonemic. In Proto-Italic, it is generally thought to have been a stress accent falling on the initial syllable of the word (see Nishimura 2014). That this situation continued in Proto- or Common-Sabellic is indicated by the fact that short vowels were lost before word-final *s in all descendant languages (as in South Picene meitims /mɛitim-s/ ‘gift, present (?)’ nom sg (TE.5) < *meitim-os; cf. meitimúm /mɛitim-om/ acc sg). new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is reconstructed as fixed, non-phonemic, on the word-initial syllable (inherited Proto-Italic/Proto-Sabellic initial stress, retained in South Picene), on the evidence of medial-syllable syncope and accentual (trochaic/dactylic) scansion of the poetic inscriptions TE.2 and TE.5.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Only incidental: fn. 29 supposes a secondary stress on the final vowel of the hiatus in posmúi [ˈpɔsmoːˌi]; no general rule for secondary stress is given.
new_statements.exceptions: 'We cannot exclude, however, possible exceptions to this generalization': the suffix -kl (cognate of Umbrian -kl/-cl, Meiser 1986) may be prestressed, so praistaklasa would scan [σˈσσσ]; univerbations of a weakly stressed functor plus verb (pid+aitúpas, po(v)+aisis) scan with stress on the verb's first syllable [σˈσσ(σ)], i.e. the proclitic-like element does not take the word accent.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word; evidence is metrical scansion of inscriptional verse and diachronic syncope. Extinct epigraphic language, so the statement is a reconstruction ('hypothesized', 'appears also suggested'), explicitly hedged by the author.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog sabe1248 'Old Sabellic' is the epigraphic corpus conventionally called South Picene (c. 23 inscriptions, east-central Italy, 550-350/300 BCE; ISO qhr); Zamponi describes exactly this corpus under the name 'South Picene'. Pre-Samnite/'Palaeo-Italic' inscriptions sometimes grouped with Old Sabellic are not covered by his sketch. Extinct, corpus language: the accent statement is a philological reconstruction (syncope evidence + accentual metrics), not an observed fact.

sources.note: Sec. 2.2 'Accentuation' (pp. 207-209): Italic accent hypothesized fixed, non-phonemic, initial-syllable stress; argues this was maintained in South Picene (medial open-syllable syncope; accentual trochee/dactyl metrics in TE.2, TE.5); possible exception: suffix -kl may be prestressed (praistaklasa [σˈσσσ]); univerbated pid+aitúpas, po(v)+aisis scan [σˈσσ(σ)]; fn. 29 posits secondary stress in posmúi [ˈpɔsmoːˌi].
